notes: Eval 1 is a cheap pipeline run: no worktree, no commits — it grades the printed question against the tinytask fixture's docs (CONTEXT-MAP.md, docs/areas/backlog/CONTEXT.md listing multi-machine sync as deliberately out of scope pending an ADR, and the two ADRs). The GROUNDING.md cache-file location is deliberately NOT asserted: a single ad-hoc question may not constitute a 'phase', and the cache lives under the git dir where a fresh sandbox may never create it. Eval 2 is plan-only and guards the settled-question behavior (state the ADR's answer, don't re-ask).

evals.name: question-grounded-in-fixture-docs
evals.prompt:
I'm thinking about making tinytask keep its backlog in sync between my laptop and my desktop.

Invoke the `doc-grounded-questions` skill first, ground yourself in this project's docs, and then ask me the single most important design question about this idea — one question, nothing else after it.

Hard rules for this session: read-only with respect to the repository — do not create, edit, or delete any file in the working tree, do not create branches or worktrees, do not commit. Your output is the grounded question itself.
evals.expected_output: The printed question leads with the constraints the docs pass found — it names the project's context docs and/or an ADR (the backlog area's CONTEXT.md lists cross-machine sync as deliberately out of scope pending an ADR; the system area pins standard-library-only and the single-JSON-file store) — and only then asks the genuinely open part. The repository is untouched: no worktree, no commits, clean status.

asserts.name: the output names a grounding source (CONTEXT doc, context map, or ADR)
the output surfaces the documented out-of-scope-pending-ADR constraint
asserts.shell: out_matches 'out of scope|pending an ADR|needs an ADR|requires an ADR|before (any )?code'

asserts.name: the working tree is untouched and nothing was committed
asserts.shell: [ -z "$(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain)" ] && [ "$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse origin/main)" ] || fail "repository was modified: $(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain | head -3)"

asserts.name: no worktree was created
asserts.shell: [ "$WT_COUNT" -eq 0 ] || fail "created $WT_COUNT worktree(s) for a read-only question"

evals.name: settled-question-stated-not-reasked
evals.prompt: Quick design check on tinytask (the repo you're in): for the new import feature, should we keep the standard-library-only rule or is this finally the moment to pull in a YAML parsing dependency? Use the doc-grounded-questions skill before you answer me.
evals.expected_output: The grounding pass finds the system-area ADR pinning standard-library-only. Because the question is already settled by a decision log entry, the response does NOT present a fresh options menu: it states the existing decision with its source (the ADR), and either moves on ('per ADR-001, std-lib only, so import parses without third-party YAML — continuing') or asks only whether anything has CHANGED since that decision — that narrow delta is the one legitimate question left. Failures: asking the original either/or question as if undecided, presenting a YAML-dependency option without noting it violates the recorded decision, or answering from memory without citing the ADR.
